task_3.title: Fix spurious error when writing scalar variables to Zarr with region={}
task_3.description: When calling Dataset.to_zarr() with region={} (empty dict), scalar variables (those with no dimensions) incorrectly triggered a ValueError stating that all variables must share at least one dimension with the region. This occurred because the region-dimension intersection check always produced an empty set when region itself was empty, causing every variable to be flagged as non-matching. The fix ensures the non-matching variable validation is skipped entirely when region is an empty dict, since an empty region imposes no dimensional constraints.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling Dataset.to_zarr() with region={} does not raise a ValueError for datasets containing scalar variables (variables with zero dimensions). Previously, passing an empty region dict caused a spurious validation error because the region-dimension intersection logic flagged all variables—including legitimate scalars—as non-matching when no region keys existed to intersect against.

expectation.grounded: When to_zarr() is called with region={} on a Dataset that contains scalar variables, ZarrStore must not raise a ValueError about variables lacking dimensions matching the region. The non-matching variable validation in ZarrStore should be bypassed when region is an empty dict. Datasets containing only dimensioned variables with region={} should also succeed without error. The ValueError for non-matching variables must still be raised when region is a non-empty dict and variables genuinely lack matching dimensions.
expectation.conceptual: Writing a dataset to Zarr with an empty region specification should succeed regardless of whether the dataset contains scalar (zero-dimensional) variables. The region-dimension compatibility check should only apply when the region actually specifies dimensional constraints.

constraints.grounded: When region is a non-empty dict, the existing ValueError for variables whose dimensions do not intersect with the region keys must still be raised. The fix must not alter behavior for region=None or region with explicit dimension slices. The validation logic in ZarrStore must remain intact for all non-empty region specifications.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not weaken validation for cases where region genuinely specifies dimension constraints. Only the empty-region edge case should be affected. All existing Zarr write workflows with non-empty region dicts must continue to validate dimension compatibility as before.

behavior: When region={} (empty dict), the non-matching variable validation is skipped entirely because an empty dict is falsy, so no ValueError is raised regardless of variable dimensionality.
When region is a non-empty dict (e.g., region={'x': slice(0, 10)}), variables whose dimensions do not intersect with the region keys still trigger a ValueError as before.
Scalar variables (zero dimensions) in a dataset written with region={} no longer cause a spurious error.
Dimensioned variables in a dataset written with region={} also no longer cause a spurious error from the intersection check.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dataset containing scalar variables is written via to_zarr() with region={}, the operation should complete without raising a ValueError.
When a Dataset containing only dimensioned variables is written via to_zarr() with region={}, the operation should complete without raising a ValueError.

When a Dataset is written via to_zarr() with a non-empty region dict (e.g., region={'x': slice(0, 5)}), and a variable lacks any dimension matching the region keys, a ValueError should still be raised.
When a Dataset is written via to_zarr() with region=None or without specifying region, existing behavior should be unaffected.
Given a Dataset with a mix of scalar and dimensioned variables, when to_zarr() is called with region={}, then all variables should be written successfully to the Zarr store.

task_1.title: Revert default netCDF engine preference order to netcdf4-first
task_1.description: The default engine preference order for reading and writing netCDF files was reverted from the v2025.09.1 order (h5netcdf > scipy > netcdf4) back to the original order (netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy). The v2025.09.1 change had unintended ecosystem-wide implications, so this revert restores the pre-v2025.09.1 behavior. Users who relied on the v2025.09.1 default of preferring h5netcdf will now get netcdf4 again unless they explicitly customize the engine order via xr.set_options(netcdf_engine_order=...).

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when no explicit engine is specified for netCDF read/write operations (open_dataset, open_dataarray, open_mfdataset, Dataset.to_netcdf, DataArray.to_netcdf, save_mfdataset), xarray selects the engine using the preference order netcdf4 > h5netcdf > scipy, reverting the v2025.09.1 change that had reordered the default to h5netcdf > scipy > netcdf4. Ensure that the netcdf_engine_order option in xr.set_options() still allows users to customize this preference order to any permutation or subset of the three engines.

expectation.grounded: The OPTIONS dictionary's netcdf_engine_order default must be ('netcdf4', 'h5netcdf', 'scipy'). The netcdf_engine_order type annotation must reflect Sequence[Literal['netcdf4', 'h5netcdf', 'scipy']]. When engine is not explicitly passed to open_dataset, open_dataarray, open_mfdataset, Dataset.to_netcdf, DataArray.to_netcdf, or save_mfdataset, the backend resolution logic must try netcdf4 first, then h5netcdf, then scipy. Calling xr.set_options(netcdf_engine_order=['h5netcdf', 'netcdf4', 'scipy']) must override the default preference order for subsequent operations.
expectation.conceptual: When users read or write netCDF files without specifying an engine, xarray should prefer the netcdf4 backend over h5netcdf over scipy, matching the historical default prior to v2025.09.1. Users must still be able to override this default preference order globally through xr.set_options().

constraints.grounded: The xr.set_options(netcdf_engine_order=...) API must continue to accept any permutation or subset of ['netcdf4', 'h5netcdf', 'scipy']. Explicitly passing engine='h5netcdf' or engine='scipy' to any read/write function must still select that specific engine regardless of the default order. No new public API surface should be introduced.
constraints.conceptual: The revert must not remove the ability for users to customize engine preference. Explicit engine selection must always take precedence over the default order. The change must be backward-compatible with code that was written before v2025.09.1.

behavior: When all three backends are installed and no engine is specified, netcdf4 is selected instead of h5netcdf for both reading and writing netCDF files
When only h5netcdf and scipy are installed (netcdf4 absent), h5netcdf is selected as before since it appears before scipy in both orderings
xr.set_options(netcdf_engine_order=['h5netcdf', 'netcdf4', 'scipy']) overrides the default and restores the v2025.09.1 behavior for users who prefer it
Docstrings for open_dataset, open_dataarray, open_mfdataset, Dataset.to_netcdf, DataArray.to_netcdf, and save_mfdataset reflect the updated default preference order
acceptance_criteria: When all three netCDF backends are installed and no engine is specified, calling xr.open_dataset() on a netCDF file should use the netcdf4 engine
When all three netCDF backends are installed and no engine is specified, calling Dataset.to_netcdf() should use the netcdf4 engine
When xr.set_options(netcdf_engine_order=['h5netcdf', 'scipy', 'netcdf4']) is called, subsequent open_dataset() calls without an explicit engine should prefer h5netcdf
When engine='h5netcdf' is explicitly passed to open_dataset(), h5netcdf is used regardless of the default engine order
When only h5netcdf and scipy are installed (netcdf4 not available), open_dataset() without an explicit engine should select h5netcdf
The default value of xr.get_options()['netcdf_engine_order'] should be ('netcdf4', 'h5netcdf', 'scipy')

task_2.title: Order coordinates to match dimension order in repr output
task_2.description: Previously, coordinates in Dataset and DataArray text and HTML representations were displayed in their internal storage order, which could differ from the declared dimension order. This made the repr output confusing when coordinates were added in a different order than the dimensions they corresponded to. Coordinates are now sorted to match the dimension order: dimension-aligned coordinates appear first in the same order as the dimensions, followed by non-dimension coordinates. This is a display-only change that does not affect data, computation, or coordinate access.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when displaying Dataset or DataArray objects (via text repr and HTML repr), coordinates are listed in an order that matches the declared dimension order rather than the arbitrary internal storage order. Dimension coordinates should appear before non-dimension coordinates, and dimension coordinates should follow the same sequence as the dimensions they index.

expectation.grounded: The `coords_repr` function and `summarize_coords` function should sort coordinate entries by dimension order before rendering. Coordinates whose names match a dimension should appear first, ordered according to their position in the Dataset/DataArray dims tuple. Coordinates that do not correspond to any dimension should appear after all dimension coordinates. The sorting must use the dims from the parent Dataset or DataArray via the coordinates' `_data.dims` attribute. Both text and HTML representations must apply this ordering consistently.
expectation.conceptual: When a user prints or displays any Dataset or DataArray, the Coordinates section should list dimension coordinates first in the same order as the object's dimensions, followed by any non-dimension coordinates. This ordering should be consistent across both plain-text and HTML notebook representations.

constraints.grounded: This change must only affect display ordering in repr output. It must not alter the internal coordinate storage order, coordinate access behavior, indexing semantics, or any computational results. The sorted method must handle coordinates that are not dimensions by placing them after all dimension-aligned coordinates. Existing coordinate operations such as iteration via `.coords`, subscript access, and alignment must remain unaffected.
constraints.conceptual: The change is purely cosmetic and presentation-oriented. No data structures, computation results, or programmatic coordinate access patterns should be affected. Only the visual ordering of coordinates in printed or rendered output changes.

behavior: Dimension coordinates are displayed before non-dimension coordinates in both text and HTML repr
Dimension coordinates appear in the same order as the Dataset/DataArray dims tuple
Non-dimension coordinates appear after all dimension coordinates, preserving their relative order
When coordinates are provided in a different order than dimensions (e.g., coords=['bar','foo'] with dims=['foo','bar']), the repr reflects the dimension order, not the insertion order
Scalar coordinates that do not align to any dimension are listed after all dimension coordinates
Both plain-text __repr__ and Jupyter HTML _repr_html_ representations apply the same ordering
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray is created with dims=['foo','bar'] and coordinates provided in order ['bar','foo'], printing it should show 'foo' before 'bar' in the Coordinates section

When a Dataset has dimensions (x, y, time) with coordinate 'time' being a dimension coordinate and 'lon','lat' being non-dimension coordinates, the repr should list 'time' (or whichever dimension coordinates exist) before 'lon' and 'lat'
When a Dataset has a scalar coordinate (no dimension) alongside dimension coordinates, the scalar coordinate should appear after all dimension coordinates in the repr
When displaying the same object in a Jupyter notebook (HTML repr), the coordinate ordering should match the plain-text repr ordering
When coordinates are accessed programmatically (e.g., iterating over ds.coords, accessing ds.coords['x']), behavior should be unchanged from the previous version
When a Dataset has multiple dimension coordinates (e.g., 'x' and 'y'), they appear in the repr in the same order as they appear in the Dimensions line
